method: All eight original PDF pages rendered with pdftoppm at 110 dpi and visually read. Compared with complete UNL transcript, including source headings, neighboring clauses and signatures. This is a human-style visual review record, not automated historical validation.

sourcePdf.textLayer: Absent; pypdf extraction returned no text on all eight pages.

pages.content: Declaration of rights and protection of persons, land and property; no folio visible.
Printed p. 10: constitutional principles, trial, impartial adjudication, opening dynastic exposition.
Printed p. 11: dynastic succession, royal prerogatives, premier office and its history.
Printed p. 12: premier coordination and governors; four island governorships and duties.
Printed p. 13: nobles, annually chosen representatives, separate/joint meetings, secretaries and decision books.
Printed p. 14: majority approval and royal/premier signatures; tax officers, notice of taxes, collection route and labor, beginning land-dispute process.
Printed p. 15: tax appeal continuation; local judges, six-person Supreme Court, final hearings, constitutional amendment provisions.
Printed p. 16: amendment continuation, assent, date 8 October 1840, Honolulu, and both signatures.

conclusion: Guide claims about record books, bilateral legislative approval and signatures, appointment and duties of tax officers, appeal routes and the six-person Supreme Court are supported by both acquired witnesses. Review does not establish implementation or the bibliographic lineage of Polaris coding.
